lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: A two-goal comeback deserved a point, but the Leafs left Seattle empty-handed - again. Brandon Montour's goal with 32.7 seconds left handed Toronto a brutal 5-4 loss to the Kraken, the club's second straight defeat after Monday's 5-2 stumble in Calgary. Toronto remains 7-6, third in the Eastern Conference with 16 points, but the margin for error is shrinking. Gavin McKenna supplied the spark with two goals and three points, while Auston Matthews tied the game late, yet Sergei Bobrovsky stopped only 12 shots and allowed the backbreaker through his pads. Coach Jim Hiller stuck with him. That decision now carries weight. A contender cannot keep surrendering winnable nights at the crease. Saturday's visit to Vancouver is the next test: watch whether Bobrovsky answers the alarm and whether Toronto can halt this two-game slide before it becomes a habit.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: Toronto's season is over, and the offseason has already exposed the central problem: a 79-83 club finishing second in the AL East needs more than one glamorous fix. Arizona Fall League prospect Aaron Parker is forcing his way into the conversation, hitting .423 with a .559 on-base percentage across 34 plate appearances - the kind of October signal that should matter when Toronto maps its next roster. Ernie Clement, meanwhile, is enjoying the other side of World Series life a year after Toronto's painful loss, a reminder that the organization still has useful, versatile pieces even if it lacks enough of them. The rotation remains the priority; injuries made stability scarce, and Dylan Cease's shoulder inflammation only sharpens that concern. Rumored interest in Tarik Skubal sounds expensive and, by Kevin Pillar's read, unlikely. Watch whether Toronto spreads its money across pitching and the outfield, rather than chasing one savior.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors needed an answer without Kawhi Leonard, and they delivered one with enough force to quiet the first alarm bells. Toronto routed Orlando 129-99 on Wednesday, turning Leonard's absence into a showcase for the young core rather than an excuse. Scottie Barnes bounced back from his scoreless performance against Minnesota with 28 points, while RJ Barrett added 25, nine rebounds and six assists. That one-two punch matters because Leonard is sidelined by swelling in his left knee and is expected to miss at least a week. Toronto is now 3-1, sits second in the Atlantic Division, and carries a one-game winning streak - a promising start, but not yet proof of durability. The Magic return Friday night at 7:30 p.m. ET. Watch whether Barnes and Barrett can repeat that authority in the rematch, because consistency without Leonard is the real test.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The bye week did not erase Washington's problems; it merely gave them time to sharpen the indictment. At 1-4-1, third in the NFC East and 2.5 games back, the Commanders are carrying a one-game losing streak into a Sunday-night reckoning. Terry McLaurin's season-ending knee injury is the latest brutal blow, stripping Jayden Daniels of his most trusted target just as the quarterback works on operating faster at the line of scrimmage. The pass rush, meanwhile, has produced only 11 sacks through six games, and Javon Kinlaw appears unlikely to face Philadelphia. There is one spark: Jer'Zhan Newton returned to practice Wednesday, opening a 21-day window for activation. Washington has a battered Eagles team in its sights, but hope requires discipline, not slogans. Sunday's 8:20 p.m. meeting with Philadelphia is the pivot - win, and the season breathes; lose, and the margin nearly vanishes.

article.title: McKenna Scores Twice as Leafs Lose to Kraken
paragraphs: Gavin McKenna scored twice and added an assist, but the Leafs lost 5-4 to the Kraken on a goal with 34 seconds left. Auston Matthews had a goal and two assists, while Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 12 shots. Toronto is listed at 7-6 and visits Vancouver on Saturday at 7:00 PM ET on Sportsnet. Kirill Marchenko is week to week, with McKenna moving onto the top line.

The Raptors handled the Magic 129-99, led by Scottie Barnes' 28 points. Toronto is 3-1 and sees Orlando again Friday at 7:30 PM ET. The Jays turn toward the Arizona Fall League, where prospects are in action, while Ernie Clement gets a different view of the World Series after last year's experience.
The Commanders, 1-4-1 and third in the NFC East, host the Eagles Sunday at 8:20 PM ET on NBC. Washington's front office is facing questions in the team's mailbag, with the game set for Sunday night.
